patterns: What should I eat to be healthy?
responses: The main food groups are fruits, vegetables, grains, protein, and dairy. Filling half your plate with fruits and veggies is a great habit.
Protein helps build and repair muscles and other parts of your body. You get it from foods like meat, fish, eggs, beans, and nuts.

patterns: How many muscles are in the body?
responses: You have more than 600 muscles. They move your body by contracting, which means getting shorter and pulling on your bones.
Your lungs bring in oxygen when you breathe in and get rid of carbon dioxide when you breathe out.
Your skin is your largest organ. It protects you, keeps you at the right temperature, and lets you feel touch.
Food gets chewed, then your stomach breaks it down with acid. Your small intestine soaks up the nutrients, and your large intestine handles the leftovers.
The immune system is your body's defense team. White blood cells find and fight germs that make you sick.

patterns: Why should I wash my hands?
How long should I wash my hands?
responses: Washing hands removes germs. Scrub with soap for about 20 seconds, about the time it takes to hum Happy Birthday twice.

patterns: How do I keep my teeth healthy?
responses: Brush twice a day for two minutes, floss daily, cut back on sugary drinks, and see a dentist regularly.

patterns: Is too much screen time bad?
responses: Lots of screen time can hurt sleep and focus. Taking breaks, going outside, and keeping screens out of bed helps.
